children: The inflows through the special foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) deposit window have crossed the $130-billion mark, with $132.9 billion coming through the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) special concessional swap window, the latest provisional data showed.

Including inflows through external commercial borrowings (ECBs) and overseas foreign currency borrowings (OFCBs), total inflows stood at $143.5 billion, significantly above market estimates of at least $90 billion.
Of the total, inflows through the ECB route stood at $5.2 billion, while those through the OFCB route came in at $5.32 billion, according to the data.

The RBI’s special concessional window for FCNR-B deposits ended on August 31. The deadline for the deposits was brought forward in mid-August from the earlier September-end deadline due to an ‘encouraging response’ from market participants, according to the central bank.

In a recent media report, Malhotra clarified that the deadline for the swap window was brought forward after “enough calibration with policymakers”, and that the decision was taken as part of external sector management.

FCNR(B) deposits are fixed-term deposits held in foreign currencies, with the principal and interest repaid in the same currency, shielding depositors from direct rupee exchange-rate risk. The arrangement allows non-resident Indians to place foreign-currency funds with Indian banks without taking direct rupee-currency risk.

The inflows provide the RBI with a larger pool of foreign currency to manage external pressures and support liquidity in the foreign-exchange market, particularly if rupee volatility intensifies. They also highlight India’s ability to tap its roughly 35-million-strong overseas diaspora for hard currency when global financial conditions become more challenging.

The RBI’s measures included absorbing hedging costs for banks mobilising FCNR(B) deposits and permitting banks to lend against the funds. The initiative was designed to strengthen India’s external-sector position and support foreign-exchange liquidity amid heightened global uncertainty.

title: RBI draws record $133 billion in forex deposits through FCNR-B window
